[0] everyday_reading (E): Everyday reading: a 'program' is a document you can save under any name, like a letter or an essay, and a misspelt word does not stop a reader from understanding it. Java rule: the file must be named exactly after its public class plus .java (HelloWorld.java for public class HelloWorld), and every character, including case and punctuation, is significant to the compiler.
[1] misconception (M) -> ClassNameMatchesFile: wrong rule: The class name and the file name are independent, so public class HelloWorld can be saved as hello.java or Program.java. Right rule: A public class Name must be saved in a file called exactly Name.java (same spelling and case).
[2] inconsistent_trace (T) -> ClassNameMatchesFile: Applies the reading rule (LT for program_text: the compiler reads the file Name.java character by character from top to bottom, ignoring comments and whitespace between tokens) unevenly: e.g. reads the code but also the comments as if they ran, or treats the file name as irrelevant on one pass and as the program name on another. (here mixing in: "class name and filename are independent")
[3] misconception (M) -> ComputerFillsInIntent: wrong rule: The computer fills in steps or values the programmer meant but did not write. Right rule: The program text is all the computer has: it executes only what the code states, so every step and value must be written.

[0] names_the_element (N): Program text (source code) is the sequence of characters typed into a text file Name.java that holds one Java program; S&W call it code.
[1] states_the_rule (S): A Java program is a sequence of characters stored in a file with a .java extension whose name matches the name after the word class on the first line (public class HelloWorld lives in HelloWorld.java).

[0] line_by_line_trace (LT): Development order: (1) edit Name.java, (2) javac Name.java translates the whole text, (3) java Name runs it. Within the text, the compiler reads tokens in order; at run time main's statements execute top to bottom.
[1] output_prediction (OP): The program text itself produces no output; its result is the file Name.class produced by javac when the text is legal, and the program's output appears only when java Name runs it.
[2] one_step_execution (OS): One edit-save of the text changes only the file Name.java; the existing Name.class (and so the behaviour of java Name) does not change until javac is run again.

[0] relation_to_neighbour (R): The name after 'public class' constrains the file name: public class Name must be in Name.java, or javac rejects it.
[1] relation_to_neighbour (R): Comments are part of the program text but are discarded when it is compiled: they may appear anywhere a whitespace may appear and never change Name.class's behaviour.
[2] relation_to_neighbour (R): javac takes the text file Name.java as input and produces Name.class; the text must be lexically and syntactically legal for any .class to be produced.
[3] purpose_of_the_whole (P): The program text is the human-readable statement of a computation: it records exactly what the computer must do so that it can be compiled, run, read and modified (copy HelloWorld.java, rename the class, replace the statements).

[0] predict_a_change (C) -> ClassNameMatchesFile: Renaming the class without renaming the file (or vice versa) breaks compilation; changing whitespace between tokens or editing comments keeps the behaviour unchanged; changing any character inside quotes changes the output.
[1] transfer_to_a_new_program (X): Use one source file per program (one public class per Name.java) and edit the text rather than the .class file; do not expect the text to carry meaning that is not written in it.
[2] diagnose_an_error (D): rule broken: public class Name must be in Name.java. Kind: compile-time. Trigger class: file name and public class name differ in spelling or case (class HelloWorld saved as Hello.java or helloworld.java)
[3] diagnose_an_error (D): rule broken: java Name runs a class, not a file name. Kind: launch error. Trigger class: typing java UseArgument.java Bob or a class name whose .class does not exist
